summaries.demographer: John Garrity is a 2-year-old non-Hispanic white male, born March 14, 2024 in Kennewick, WA, who has lived his entire life in the Creekstone neighborhood of south Kennewick (Q85, Q87, Q08). He resides in an owned, middle-class home with two college-educated, married biological parents — Mark, a mechanical engineer in operations support at Energy Northwest, and Sarah, a part-time library aide at Mid-Columbia Library District — placing the household squarely in the dual-income professional middle class of the Tri-Cities region (Q58, Q100, Q101, Q106, Q107). He is an only child currently enrolled in part-time preschool at Little Sprouts Learning Center (M/W/F mornings), with full pediatric coverage via his father's employer-sponsored insurance (Q15, Q36, Q92). Religiously, the family identifies as non-denominational Christian and attends Bethel Church in Richland (Q47, Q94), and politically the household is moderate-mixed with independent-leaning voting behavior in a region shaped by Hanford- and Energy-Northwest-driven scientific professional employment (Q24, Q95).
summaries.behavioral_economist: John exhibits an unusually strong preference for routine, predictability, and ordered environments for a child his age — sorting blocks by color and size, lining up his shoes, and reacting with strong loss aversion when his 'Bee-Bee' blanket went missing for two days (Q01, Q03, Q43, Q44). His choice architecture is heavily scaffolded by his parents, who themselves are explicitly spreadsheet-driven decision-makers (sinking funds, 529 plans, four-month emergency fund, deliberate part-time daycare optimization), and these scaffolds appear to be cultivating similar preference patterns in him (Q02, Q03, Q60, Q61). He responds well to small extrinsic incentives — raisins as cleanup motivation, the 'Clean Up, Clean Up' song as a behavioral nudge — while also displaying intrinsic motivation around mastery tasks like puzzles, towers, and helping with chores (Q17). His time preference is, predictably for a two-year-old, present-focused, but the household environment is steeply future-oriented around him: 529 contributions, planned 2029 Disneyland trip, swim lessons, and a deliberate sibling pipeline (Q61, Q108).
summaries.political_scientist: John has no personal political identity at age 2, but his civic socialization is already underway: he accompanied his mother to drop a ballot at the library in November 2025, attends a Fourth of July block party on his cul-de-sac, and is being raised in a household that votes in every general election by Washington's vote-by-mail system (Q08, Q23). His political environment is what one might call 'moderate-mixed independent' — a Republican-leaning engineer father and Democrat-leaning librarian mother who deliberately avoid yard signs, avoid partisan talk in front of him, and have shifted toward local civic engagement (school board, utility issues) since becoming parents (Q24, Q25, Q95). Institutional trust in the household is high — toward pediatricians, the CDC, public libraries, and the public utility — and law-enforcement experience is benign, limited to a positive Officer Lopez safety visit at preschool (Q20, Q42). John is growing up in a community with significant Pacific Northwest scientific-professional demographics, and his early peer environment (Hispanic, Vietnamese-American, white classmates and neighbors) is intentionally being framed by his parents as the diverse default rather than the exception (Q28).
summaries.psychologist: John presents as a temperamentally easy child with strong order-seeking traits, robust attachment to both parents, and developmentally-appropriate emotion regulation buttressed by stable routines and a transitional object — his blue 'Bee-Bee' blanket — that anchors his self-soothing (Q01, Q03, Q43, Q44). He shows precocious agreeableness in peer settings (parallel play with Ellie, tolerating bossy cousin Mia, gentle behavior with the cat) while still expressing typical toddler assertiveness around routines like 'Daddy do it' at bath time (Q05, Q07, Q11). His cognitive style is observational and categorical — sorting, lining up, and labeling — paired with a rich symbolic-play repertoire (firefighter helmet, butterfly drawings) suggestive of healthy theory-of-mind emergence (Q01, Q65, seed). Relationally, he attaches not just to caregivers but to specific institutional figures like Miss Jenna and Miss Patty, indicating a secure-attachment template generalizing to non-family adults (Q07). His motivational architecture is layered: mastery needs around order and competence, affiliative needs met by abundant family and peer interaction, and emerging autonomy expressed through chores and clothing preferences — a profile that combines reliability with the curiosity his parents most hope to nurture (Q15, Q17, Q108).
